name: Plane
tagline: Open source project management with issues, cycles, modules and kanban views, aimed at teams that want a Jira alternative.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A personal issue tracker is one of the most one-shottable products there is: a table of issues, a few states, drag and drop, and a filter bar. If you are the only person using it, most of Plane's surface area (workspaces, roles, permissions, activity feeds, notifications) is dead weight you never touch. What you cannot one-shot is the collaboration layer: real time updates, comment threads, GitHub and Slack sync, and the shared vocabulary that makes a team actually look at the board. Worth saying out loud: Plane ships a free self-hostable community edition, so the honest comparison for a solo user is your weekend build versus running theirs with docker compose. Build it anyway if you want something that boots in a second and stores everything in one SQLite file you can grep.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you create issues with state, priority, labels and a markdown description, drag them across a kanban board, group them into cycles, and filter or search the whole backlog.
requirements: A folder you are willing to back up, since the SQLite file is the whole product
whatYouLose: Multiplayer: no real time board, no assignees who are not you, no comments anyone reads
GitHub, GitLab and Slack sync, so issues never close themselves from a commit message
Mobile apps and a hosted URL you can open from a phone on the train
Polish accumulated over years: saved views, sub-issues, estimates, keyboard shortcuts that already feel right
Someone else's problem when the database corrupts or the migration breaks
moatNotes: The moat is other people using the same board, which is exactly the thing a personal build cannot have.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for Plane Cloud for the same reason they pay for any tracker: they do not want to be the sysadmin for the place their team's work lives, and they want the GitHub sync, invites, permissions and uptime to be someone else's job. Solo users mostly do not pay, and Plane knows this, which is why the community edition exists. The paid tiers are a team purchase, and once three people have opinions about cycles and views, a hand rolled kanban stops being charming.
notes: Solo issue trackers are the hello world of side projects, which is why everyone has abandoned four of them.
prompt:
Build a local, single user issue tracker called Hangar. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind for styling
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/hangar.db, created and migrated on first boot
- dnd-kit for drag and drop
- No external services, no auth, no analytics. Nothing leaves localhost.

Data model:
- project: id, name, key (short prefix like HGR), archived flag
- issue: id, project_id, seq (per project counter so ids read HGR-14), title, description (markdown), state (backlog, todo, in_progress, done, cancelled), priority (none, low, medium, high, urgent), cycle_id nullable, created_at, updated_at, closed_at nullable
- label: id, project_id, name, color; issue_label join table
- cycle: id, project_id, name, start_date, end_date

Screens:
1. Board: kanban columns by state, drag cards between columns to update state, optimistic UI, cards show id, title, priority dot, labels
2. List: dense table with sortable columns and a filter bar (state, priority, label, cycle, free text search over title and description)
3. Issue detail: editable title, markdown description with live preview, state and priority selects, label picker, cycle assignment, created/updated timestamps, delete with confirm
4. Cycles: create a cycle, see its issues, show a simple done vs open count and a progress bar
5. Settings: create and rename projects, manage labels, export everything as JSON, import that same JSON back

Behavior details:
- Keyboard: "c" opens a quick create modal, "/" focuses search, "escape" closes modals
- Quick create parses inline syntax: "!high" sets priority, "#label" attaches or creates a label
- Setting state to done or cancelled stamps closed_at; moving back out clears it
- Everything server side via route handlers or server actions, no client side ORM

Explicitly out of scope: users, invites, permissions, comments, notifications, email, GitHub or Slack integration, real time sync, mobile app, sub issues, time estimates.

Deliver: working app on npm run dev at localhost:3000, seeded with one project and about a dozen sample issues, plus a README covering setup, where the db file lives, and how to back it up.
